part2.intro: Three young people talk about a holiday when the weather was important.
part2.question: For each question, choose the correct answer.

texts.label: A
texts.title: Tomás
texts.text: Last summer my family went to Morocco. It was the hottest place I've ever been – forty-two degrees on some days! We got up at six every morning to visit places before it got too hot, and in the afternoons we rested in our hotel room. One night we slept in a tent in the desert. I've never seen so many stars. I'd love to go back, but in spring next time.

texts.label: B
texts.title: Isla
texts.text: In February I went to Iceland with my mum and my older sister. It was really cold and there was snow everywhere. On the third day there was a terrible storm, and our flight home was cancelled, so we had to stay two more days. I didn't mind at all! On the last night we saw the Northern Lights. My sister took some amazing photos, and one of them won a competition.

texts.label: C
texts.title: Kenji
texts.text: My cousins and I went walking in the mountains in Wales in October. On the first day it was sunny and warm, and we could see the sea from the top. But the next morning it was so foggy that we couldn't see the path. Our guide decided we should go back down. I was a bit disappointed, but he was right. Then it rained for the rest of the week, so we visited museums.

items.q: Who changed their daily routine because of the weather?
Who got home later than planned?
Who had better weather at the start of the holiday than later?
Whose family member won a prize?
Who would like to visit the same place at a different time of year?
Who agreed with a decision that someone else made?
Who spent a night in an unusual place?

part3.title: Life on a windy island
part3.text:
Twelve-year-old Finn MacLeod lives on Skerra, a small island off the coast of Scotland. Only forty people live there, and Finn is one of just six children.

The weather is the most important thing in Finn's life. There's no secondary school on the island, so every Monday morning he takes a small boat to the mainland, where he stays with his aunt until Friday. "If the sea is calm, the journey takes forty minutes," he says. "But when it's windy, the waves are huge, and I feel really sick."

In winter, storms sometimes stop the boat for days. Last January, Finn couldn't get home for two weeks. "I missed my family a lot," he says. "But my aunt was great, and I did lots of homework, so my teachers were happy!"

When he's at home, Finn helps his grandfather, who has a small farm with sheep. Before they go out, they always check the sky. "Grandpa doesn't use a weather app," Finn laughs. "He looks at the clouds and the birds, and he's nearly always right."

People often ask Finn if he'd prefer to live in a city. "No way," he says. "In summer, when it's sunny, the island is the most beautiful place in the world. You can swim with seals! And in winter, when the wind is shouting outside, our kitchen is so warm and cosy. I'd never change it."

items.q: Why does Finn leave the island during the week?
options: His parents work on the mainland.
He has to go to school.
He helps his aunt with her work.

items.q: What does Finn say about the boat journey?
options: He enjoys it most when it is windy.
It always takes the same time.
It is unpleasant in bad weather.

items.q: What happened last January?
options: Finn could not travel home for a long time.
Finn's teachers were angry with him.
Finn's aunt was ill for two weeks.

items.q: How does Finn's grandfather know what the weather will be?
How does Finn feel about living on the island?
options: He would like to move to a city.
He loves it in every season.
He only enjoys it in summer.

part4.title: Thunder and lightning
part4.text:
Every second, around the world, lightning hits the ground about one hundred {19}. Most of these flashes come from thunderstorms, which are most {20} in hot, wet countries.

Thunderstorms happen when warm air goes up quickly into the sky and meets cold air. Big, dark clouds form, and soon there is heavy rain, strong wind and lightning. We hear the thunder after we see the lightning because light {21} faster than sound.

Lightning can be very dangerous, so it is important to {22} safe during a storm. If you are outside, go into a building or a car as quickly as possible. Don't stand under a tree, and get out of the water if you are swimming.

Scientists say that a person has about a one-in-a-million {23} of being hit by lightning. But one American park ranger, Roy Sullivan, was hit seven times between 1942 and 1977 – and each time he {24} better again!

Greetings from Italy! The weather here is great – it's been sunny {25} day and it's much hotter {26} at home. Yesterday we went to the beach and I swam in the sea. Tomorrow we're going {27} visit Rome. What's the weather like there?
Olivia

Hi Olivia,
Lucky you! It's been raining here {28} three days. I wanted to go to the park, but I couldn't go because {29} the rain. Mum says it will be sunny on Sunday, so I hope she's right. Have a great time in Rome and send me {30} photos!

grey clouds; it is snowing and the boy on his bike looks very cold

part7.model: On Saturday morning it was sunny, so Ben went to see his friend Sam by bike. He only wore a T-shirt. But on the way, the sky became cloudy and it started to snow. Ben was very cold when he arrived. Sam's mum gave him a warm scarf and a hot drink.

items.q: What was the weather like at the girl's party?

script.t: How was your birthday party in the garden, Nadia?
Well, the forecast said it would be sunny, so we planned to eat outside.
And did it rain?
No, luckily it stayed dry. And there wasn't any sun – it was cloudy and so windy! The paper plates flew all over the garden.

items.q: Which activity is cancelled today?

script.t: Has everyone got their life jackets? Oh, wait. Sorry, everyone. There's a thunderstorm coming, so there's no sailing on the lake today.
Oh no! Can we go horse riding instead?
Yes, riding is still happening at two o'clock. And climbing is on the indoor wall, so that's happening too.
Great. I'll do climbing, then.

items.q: What has the boy forgotten?

script.t: Have you got everything for the beach, Sam? It's going to be really sunny today.
Yes, Mum. I've got my sunglasses on already, and my cap's in the car.
Did you pack the sun cream?
Oh no, I didn't! I'll get it from the bathroom.

items.q: What is the temperature now?

script.t: It's cold this morning! The radio said it's only five degrees.
That was at seven o'clock. It's warmer now – the thermometer in the garden says fifteen.
Will it get warmer this afternoon?
Not much. The forecast says it'll be twenty-five tomorrow, but not today.

items.q: How will the boy get to school today?

script.t: Mum, can I cycle to school today? It's sunny.
The roads are still icy after last night. It isn't safe on a bike.
Can you drive me, then?
Sorry, I've got to be at work early. Take the bus – it stops right outside the school.

part2.intro: You will hear a woman talking on the radio about a kite festival.
part2.title: Kite Festival

items.label: If there's a thunderstorm, the festival will move to:

script.t: And now, what's on this weekend. If you enjoy windy weather, don't miss the Kite Festival at Polwick Beach. That's P-O-L-W-I-C-K. It's just ten minutes from the town centre by bus. The festival opens on Saturday at half past ten. Last year it started at nine, but people said that was too early! There'll be kites of every colour and size – some are as big as a bus. Last year adult tickets were six pounds, but this year they only cost four pounds, and children under twelve can go for free. Now, the weather. The forecast for Saturday is good – sunny with strong winds, which is perfect for kites. But if there's a thunderstorm, it isn't safe to fly kites, so the festival will move to Sunday. Please don't bring an umbrella – the wind is too strong for umbrellas on the beach! It can get quite cold by the sea, even when it's sunny, so remember to bring a jacket. You can buy food and drink at the festival café. For more information, visit the festival website.

part3.intro: You will hear Mia talking to her friend Alex about a science project on the weather.

items.q: Why did Alex choose fog for his project?
options: His teacher gave him the topic.
His father had a problem because of fog.
He saw fog when he was on a plane.

items.q: How is Alex going to present his project?
options: as a talk to the class

items.q: What is Mia using to measure the rain?
When must the students finish their projects?
When will Mia and Alex go to the library?

script.t: Hi Alex. Have you started the science project yet?
Yes, I have. Mr Grant said we could choose any topic about the weather, so I'm doing mine on fog.
Fog? Why?

Well, I wanted to do snow first, but three other people chose it. Then my dad told me about a day when he was flying home and his plane couldn't land because of fog. He had to wait at another airport for six hours! So I got interested.
Cool. What are you going to do for it?
I'm going to make a big poster. I thought about making a video, but my camera's broken. What's your topic?
Rain. I'm measuring how much rain falls in our garden every day for a month. I made the thing to measure it from an old plastic bottle.
Has it rained much?
Not at all! It's been sunny for ten days. My little brother keeps asking when it's going to rain, because he wants to play in the puddles.
Ha! When do we have to give the projects to Mr Grant?
On the fifteenth. That's Friday next week. Oh – no, sorry, he changed it. It's Monday the eighteenth now.
Good, I need more time. Are you going to the library after school? I need some books about fog.
I can't today – I've got swimming. But I can go tomorrow.
OK, let's go tomorrow, then.

items.intro: You will hear a boy talking about a day at the beach.
items.q: How did he feel at the end of the day?

script.t: We went to the beach on Sunday. The morning was cloudy and a bit cold, so at first I was disappointed. But at lunchtime the sun came out and it got really warm. We swam, played volleyball and ate ice cream. By the evening I was so happy that I didn't want to go home!

items.intro: You will hear a girl talking to her father.
items.q: What does the girl want her father to do?
options: drive her to her friend's house

script.t: Dad, it's raining really hard and I'm meeting Lucy at her house at four.
Take my big umbrella – it's by the door.
It's too windy for an umbrella. It'll break! Could you take me there in the car? It's only five minutes.
OK, go and get your coat.

items.intro: You will hear a weather presenter on TV.
items.q: What is the presenter's main message?
options: Schools will close because of snow.
The afternoon will be cold and wet.
People should drive carefully in the morning.

script.t: Good evening. Tonight it'll be very cold, and by tomorrow morning there will be thick fog in many places, especially near rivers. If you're driving to work or school, please go slowly and turn your lights on. The fog should go by lunchtime, and the afternoon will be dry and sunny. There's no snow yet – but it might come next week.

items.intro: You will hear two friends talking about a football match.
items.q: Why was the match stopped?

script.t: How was the match on Saturday?

Well, it was raining when we started, but that was OK – we often play in the rain. Then in the second half we heard thunder and saw lightning over the hills, so the referee stopped the game. We were winning two-nil!
That's bad luck.

items.intro: You will hear a girl talking about her favourite season.
items.q: Why does she like autumn?
options: She can wear her favourite clothes.
She enjoys the colours of the trees.

script.t: Most of my friends love summer, but autumn is my favourite season. It's still quite warm in September, and I don't mind the cold, foggy days in November either. But the best thing is walking through the park when all the leaves are red, orange and yellow. It's so beautiful. I always take lots of photos.

part5.intro: You will hear Leo talking to his grandmother about his week at an activity camp. What did he do on each day?

script.t: Hi Leo! How was the activity camp?
Great, Grandma! But the weather changed every day, so we didn't always do what we planned.
What happened on Monday?
It was really sunny and hot, so we went swimming in the lake all afternoon. We were going to play football, but it was too hot to run around.
Very sensible. And Tuesday?
On Tuesday it was so foggy that we couldn't see the other side of the lake. So no canoeing! We did climbing on the indoor wall instead.
And Wednesday?
Wednesday was cloudy but dry, and there was no wind at all, so we finally went canoeing. I fell in the water twice!
Oh, Leo! What about Thursday?
There was a big thunderstorm in the morning and it rained all day. Some people did drawing, but I chose the cooking class. We made pizza!
Lovely. And on the last day?
The sun came back, but it was windy and quite cold. We went for a long walk in the hills. I wanted to go fishing, but there wasn't time.
It sounds wonderful.
